title: List of All Banks in India 2026: Complete RBI Official List
summary: Complete list of all banks in India from the official RBI list: public sector, private, small finance, payments, foreign, RRBs and co-operative banks.
body_markdown:
India's banking system is organised by the Reserve Bank of India into clear categories, each with its own licence type and role: public sector banks owned by the government, private sector banks, small finance banks for underserved customers, payments banks for deposits and payments, foreign banks, regional rural banks, and co-operative banks. This article presents the complete **list of all banks in India** , category by category, compiled from the RBI's official published list.


## Banks in India at a Glance


Category Count What they are


Public Sector Banks 12 Government-majority banks including SBI


Private Sector Banks 21 Indian privately owned commercial banks


Small Finance Banks 11 Full banks focused on small customers and MSMEs


Payments Banks 5 Deposits and payments, no lending


Foreign Banks 44 Overseas banks operating in India


Regional Rural Banks 28 State-level rural banks sponsored by PSBs


State Co-operative Banks 34 Apex co-operative banks of states and UTs

## Other Co-operative Banks


Beyond the state apex banks, the RBI also regulates scheduled and non-scheduled urban co-operative banks and district central co-operative banks. These number in the hundreds and change more frequently; the complete current lists are maintained on the RBI website.


## How to Verify Any Bank


1. Visit the RBI website's list of banks in India section.
2. Match the exact legal name of the bank, not just a similar-sounding brand.
3. For deposits (see[how to open a savings account](https://gromo.in/blog/how-to-open-a-savings-account/) ), remember DICGC insurance covers up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank, and it applies to commercial banks, small finance banks, payments banks, and eligible co-operative banks.
4. Be cautious with entities using bank-like names without an RBI licence (the same verification habit behind our[RBI approved loan apps list](https://gromo.in/blog/rbi-approved-loan-apps/) ); only institutions on these lists may accept public deposits as banks.


## FAQ: List of Banks in India


**How many banks are there in India?**


Per the RBI's official list, India has 12 public sector banks, 21 private sector banks, 2 local area banks, 11 small finance banks, 5 payments banks, 44 foreign banks, 28 regional rural banks, and 34 state co-operative banks: 157 institutions across these categories, plus hundreds of urban and district co-operative banks that the RBI lists separately.


**Which is the largest bank in India?**


State Bank of India is the largest bank in India by assets, branches, and customers, headquartered in Mumbai. Among private sector banks, HDFC Bank is the largest, followed by ICICI Bank and Axis Bank.


**What is the difference between public and private sector banks?**


Ownership. In public sector banks the government holds the majority stake (SBI and 11 nationalised banks). Private sector banks are majority-owned by private shareholders. Both are regulated identically by the RBI, and deposits in both carry the same DICGC insurance of up to Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank.


**Are small finance banks and payments banks safe?**


Yes, within their design. Small finance banks are full RBI-licensed banks whose deposits carry DICGC insurance up to Rs 5 lakh, the same as any commercial bank. Payments banks are also RBI-licensed and insured, but can hold deposits only up to Rs 2 lakh per customer and cannot lend. Safety comes from the licence, not the size.


**How many regional rural banks are there in India now?**


28, following the amalgamation that consolidated RRBs into broadly one per state. Each RRB is sponsored by a public sector bank and focuses on rural and agricultural banking, such as Bihar Gramin Bank, Karnataka Grameena Bank, and Uttar Pradesh Gramin Bank.


## Disclaimer


This list is compiled from the[Reserve Bank of India's official published list of banks](https://www.rbi.org.in/commonman/english/scripts/BanksInIndia.aspx?ref=gromo.in) and reflects it at the time of writing. Bank mergers, new licences, licence cancellations, and name changes occur periodically, so always verify the current status of any bank on the RBI website before making decisions.
